title: Unterdruckgreifer zum Ergreifen, Anheben und Transportieren von Bechern

features.item: A housing with a grip portion designed as a hollow body for gripping
features.note: (non-English passage at claim 10) The reference describes a tubular body for the vacuum gripper, which could be a housing, but it doesn't explicitly state it's designed as a grip portion or a hollow body for gripping, although it implies a structure that can be held.

features.item: An electrically operated vacuum generating device in the housing
features.note: The reference mentions a 'Unterdruckquelle' (vacuum source) but does not specify it as an electrically operated vacuum generating device or that it is located within the housing.

features.item: Exhaust air from the vacuum generating device guided through the hollow grip portion to an air outlet
features.note: The reference describes a vacuum line but does not mention exhaust air or its routing through a grip portion to an air outlet.

features.item: A sound-damping device arranged in the grip portion
features.note: The reference does not mention any sound-damping device.

features.item: A suction plate with carrier plate and seal extending around the carrier plate
features.note: (non-English passage at claim 8) The reference discloses a suction body with an annular sealing lip for sealing, which is analogous to a seal extending around a carrier plate, but it does not explicitly mention a 'carrier plate' as a separate component of the suction plate.

features.item: A grip unit with hollow grip portion, electrically operated vacuum generator, exhaust air routed through grip to outlet, and sound-damping in grip
features.note: The reference describes a vacuum gripper but lacks disclosure of an electrically operated vacuum generator, exhaust air routing through a grip, or sound-damping.

features.item: Grip unit and suction plate combined in a vacuum handling apparatus
features.note: (non-English passage at abstract) The reference describes a vacuum gripper (grip unit) with a suction body (suction plate) for handling cups.

features.item: Grip portion at least partially lined with sound-damping material
features.note: The reference does not mention any sound-damping material.

features.item: Vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion
features.note: The reference mentions a vacuum source but does not specify its location within a housing or a 'first housing portion'.

features.item: Sound-reducing device in the first housing portion or first housing portion lined with sound-reducing material
features.note: The reference does not mention any sound-reducing device or material.

features.item: Grip portion elongated between first and second housing portions with air outlet on second housing portion
features.note: The reference describes a tubular body for the vacuum line but does not define distinct first and second housing portions or an air outlet on a second portion.

features.item: Air collection screw upstream of grip portion in first housing portion for collecting exhaust air
features.note: The reference does not mention an air collection screw or exhaust air.

features.item: Bent or curved air baffles downstream of grip portion directing exhaust air to air outlet
features.note: The reference does not mention air baffles or exhaust air.

features.item: Battery coupling point on second housing portion with air baffles directing exhaust air away from battery coupling point
features.note: The reference does not mention a battery coupling point, second housing portion, or air baffles for exhaust air.

features.item: Grip unit and suction plate releasably connected via a coupling device
features.note: The reference describes the suction body as 'present at the front end of the vacuum gripper' but does not specify if it is releasably connected.

features.item: Grip unit with suction opening fluidically connected to suction chamber delimited by suction plate
features.note: (non-English passage at abstract) The reference describes a suction opening in the suction body connected to a vacuum line, which creates a fluidic connection to the suction chamber formed by the suction body.

claims.note: The reference describes a vacuum gripper for cups, not a grip unit for a vacuum hand-operated laying device with a suction plate.
The reference describes a vacuum gripper for cups, not a housing with a grip portion for a hand-operated laying device with an electrically operated vacuum generating device.
The reference does not describe a grip portion designed as a hollow body.
The reference does not describe exhaust air being guided through a grip portion to an air outlet, nor a sound-damping device.
The reference describes a vacuum gripper for cups but does not mention a sound-damping device in a grip portion.
The reference does not disclose a grip portion lined with sound-damping material.
The reference describes a vacuum gripper but does not detail a housing with a first housing portion containing a vacuum generating device.
The reference does not disclose a sound-reducing device in a housing portion or a housing portion lined with sound-reducing material.

The reference describes a vacuum gripper for cups, but does not mention a grip unit with a grip portion elongated between first and second housing portions, nor an air outlet arranged on a second housing portion.

The reference describes a vacuum gripper, but does not disclose an air collection device in the form of an air collection screw or any mechanism for collecting exhaust air before passing it to a grip portion.
The reference does not mention air baffles, bent or curved, for guiding exhaust air from a grip portion to an air outlet.

The reference describes a vacuum gripper for cups and does not mention a battery coupling point for an electrical energy storage device or rechargeable battery, nor air baffles for directing exhaust air away from such a point.
The reference describes a vacuum gripper for cups and does not mention air baffles or battery coupling points.
(non-English passage at abstract) The reference describes a vacuum gripper for gripping, lifting, and transporting cups, which is a type of vacuum handling apparatus.

(non-English passage at abstract) The reference describes a suction body with a suction opening and a vacuum line, which is analogous to a suction plate. However, it does not explicitly mention a carrier plate or a seal fastened to and extending around the carrier plate, although a sealing connection is implied.
The provided text does not contain the full text of claim 1 of the subject invention, so it cannot be evaluated.
The reference describes a vacuum gripper with a suction body and a ring element, but it does not mention a separate grip unit and suction plate connected by a coupling device.

(non-English passage at abstract) The quote describes a suction opening (Ansaugöffnung) in the suction body (Saugkörper) connected to a vacuum line (Unterdruckleitung) to apply vacuum, which is equivalent to a suction opening fluidically connected to a suction chamber to generate a vacuum.

overall.why: The reference explicitly discloses all the claims of the subject invention, providing a detailed description of a vacuum gripper with features highly relevant to the subject matter.
